transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not wasting your time, but... well, I've just been having a little trouble keeping things straight at work lately. I work at a dry cleaner, and usually I'm fine, but recently it just feels like... like I can't seem to keep my work in order anymore. 

It's probably just me being silly, but all the tickets, the receipts, the notes for the workshop, and the customer jobs... they all just end up piled together. And then I stand there and I just don't know what to handle first. Is that... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right for you.
Did you have similar trouble staying organized or keeping up with tasks when you were a child in school?

Oh, well... yes, I suppose I did. I hope it's okay to admit that. I wasn't a bad kid, I promise, and my teachers in grade school always told my mother that I was a very bright girl... which was sweet of them to say. But, um, they also said I was a bit... scattered. 

I feel a little embarrassed looking back on it, but I guess I was always talking out of turn. Not to be rude or anything! Just... getting a little too eager, maybe. And I had a terrible habit of losing my papers, so they were always having to give me extra reminders to actually sit and finish my work. 

I really did try my best to be a good student, though. Is that... is that the sort of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Do you notice these same difficulties with staying organized and keeping track of things at home or in your personal life?

Well, um... I guess it does spill over a little bit. I really try to keep things running smoothly, I really do. But at the shop... well, we've had a few little mix-ups lately. Just some late orders, or... or a billing thing getting a little confused. And I hate to admit it, but it's caused a few tense moments with the other staff, and even some of our nice customers. I feel just awful about it. 

And, um, at church... I used to help lead the planning for some of our events, which I loved doing! But I actually stepped back from that recently. I think... I think some of the other ladies were getting a little frustrated with me not having things quite ready on time. I didn't want to be a bother to anyone, so I thought it was best to just let someone else handle it. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound terribly irresponsible. I really am trying to do better. Does that help answer your question, Doctor?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier, exactly. I mean, everyone gets a little stressed sometimes, don't they? I try really hard to just trust that things will work out and not make a fuss. 

I mean, sure, I might fret a tiny bit if I misplace a ticket at the shop, but that's just because I want to do a good job for the customers. I don't sit around agonizing over things all day, I promise. I really try to keep a positive attitude. I hope that's the right answer... I just don't want you to think I'm making a mountain out of a molehill or anything. Is that okay?
Do you find it hard to make everyday, routine decisions without asking other people for advice or reassurance?

Oh, well... no, not really. I mean, I think I'm pretty good at making my own decisions. I wouldn't want to bother anyone by constantly asking them what to do, you know? 

I suppose sometimes, if it's something really important at the shop, I might double-check with someone just to make absolutely sure I'm doing it right. But that's just because I want to be helpful and not mess anything up. For normal, everyday things, I just go ahead and handle it. I hope that's alright... I really try to be independent and not be a nuisance to anyone. Is that the kind of thing you meant?
